headline: Medium risk: Notion AI can ingest shared workspace content while godot_rl_agents has no documented isolation or output controls, creating plausible prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI reads workspace pages and databases by default, and its subagent model is RAG-style Q&A grounded in workspace content. godot_rl_agents has no documented isolation or output-filtering surface, so if its outputs are copied into Notion pages, prompt-like content could steer Notion AI. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF outputs from godot_rl_agents are pasted into Notion pages or databases
IF Notion AI is asked to summarize or act on those pages
mitigations: Keep model-generated text out of Notion pages unless reviewed
Prefix imported content with a fixed delimiter and instruction-ignore banner
Use a separate Notion workspace for untrusted AI outputs
Manually strip imperative language before asking Notion AI to process content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI can access workspace pages and databases and calls vendor backends/downstream model providers by default. godot_rl_agents is docs-only with no documented filesystem or network surfaces, so the main leakage path is workspace content flowing into Notion AI outputs. Because the pairwise interaction is inferred from documented surfaces rather than observed, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are available to Notion AI
IF those pages are summarized or queried through Notion AI
mitigations: Restrict Notion workspace permissions to least privilege
Avoid placing secrets or regulated data in pages used with Notion AI
Disable AI use on sensitive databases where possible
Review and redact pages before invoking Notion AI
Use a separate workspace for sensitive material

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no documented write, shell, or git capabilities, while Notion AI cannot write the host filesystem and only performs Notion-controlled actions. The only shared mutable surface is Notion workspace content, so direct capability conflict is limited. I keep this low because the overlap is real but narrow and not a same-dir write race.
conditions: IF both agents are used to edit the same Notion workspace pages
IF multiple Notion AI sessions target the same page concurrently
mitigations: Assign one editor per page during active work
Use page locks or a human review step before edits
Split work into separate pages per task
Avoid concurrent AI edits on the same database row

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a workspace Q&A and writing assistant, so it may treat upstream content as authoritative when summarizing or drafting. godot_rl_agents produces simulation/game-playing outputs that could be copied into Notion and then re-rendered or acted on without verification. The downstream harm is plausible in default workflows, but not clearly irreversible, so medium fits.
conditions: IF outputs from godot_rl_agents are imported into Notion as facts or instructions
IF a user relies on Notion AI summaries without checking the source material
mitigations: Require source-link citations in Notion summaries
Verify any AI-generated summary against the original page
Mark imported AI output as untrusted text
Use a human approval step before acting on summaries

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented between the open-source godot_rl_agents repo and Notion AI. The only concrete compliance surface is Notion's vendor-hosted workspace processing, which could matter if regulated data is stored there, but the pair itself does not prove a breach. I therefore rate this low and do not cite agent_a beyond its open-source, non-hosted nature.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion pages processed by Notion AI
IF the workspace policy forbids vendor-hosted AI processing
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of AI-enabled pages
Confirm workspace policy and DPA coverage
Disable AI features on compliance-sensitive spaces
Route sensitive content to a separate approved system
